{{Short description|Cadlag in probability theory}}
An '''additive process''', in [[probability theory]], is a [[cadlag]], [[Continuous stochastic process#Continuity in probability|continuous in probability]] [[stochastic process]] with [[independent increments]].
An additive process is the generalization of a [[Lévy process]] (a Lévy process is an additive process with stationary increments). An example of an additive process that is not a Lévy process is a [[Brownian motion]] with a time-dependent drift.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=455}}
The additive process was introduced by [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]] in 1937.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=468}}

There are applications of the additive process in [[quantitative finance]]{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=454}} (this family of processes can capture important features of the [[implied volatility]]) and in [[digital image processing]].{{sfn|Bhattacharya|Brockwell|1976|p= 71}}

== Definition ==
An additive process is a generalization of a Lévy process obtained relaxing the hypothesis of stationary increments. Thanks to this feature an additive process can describe more complex phenomenons than a  Lévy process.

A [[stochastic process]] <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> on <math>\mathbb R^d</math> such that  <math>X_0=0 </math> almost surely is an additive process if it satisfy the following hypothesis:
#It has independent increments.
#It is continuous in probability.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=455}}

== Main properties ==
=== Independent increments ===
A stochastic process <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> has independent increments if and only if for any <math>0\leq p<r\leq s<t </math>  the random variable <math>X_t-X_s</math> is independent from the random variable <math>X_r-X_p</math>.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=80}}{{what|reason=This seems quite wrong. It is only pairwise independence. Actually, we need mutual independent for any finite number of disjoint intervals. This is well-described in the Wikipedia article on Levy processes.|date=August 2023}}

=== Continuity in probability ===
A stochastic process <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> is continuous in probability if, and only if, for any <math>t>0</math>
:<math>\lim_{s \to t^-} \Pr \left(\big|  X_s- X_t \big| \geq \varepsilon \right) = 0.</math>{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=80}}

== Lévy–Khintchine representation ==
There is a strong link between additive process and [[infinitely divisible distribution]]s. An additive process at time <math>t</math> has an infinitely divisible distribution characterized by the generating triplet <math>(\gamma_t, A_t, \nu_t)</math>. <math> \gamma_t</math> is a vector in <math>\mathbb R^d</math>, <math> A_t</math> is a matrix in <math>\mathbb R^{d\times d}</math> and  <math>\nu_t</math> is a measure on <math>\mathbb R^d</math> such that 
<math>\nu_t(\{0\})=0 </math> and <math>\int_{\mathbb R^d}(1\wedge x^2)\nu_t(dx)<\infty</math>. {{sfn|Sato|1999|p=47}}

<math> \gamma_t</math> is called drift term, <math> A_t</math> covariance matrix and  <math>\nu_t</math> Lévy measure.
It is possible to write explicitly the additive process characteristic function using the ''Lévy–Khintchine formula'':

: <math>\varphi_X(u)(t) := \operatorname E \left[e^{iu'X_t}\right] = \exp \left(u' \gamma_t i - \frac{1}{2}u' A_t u + \int_{\mathbb R^d} \left(e^{i u' x}-1 -iu'x\mathbf{I}_{|x|<1}\right)\,\nu_t(dx) \right),
</math>

where <math>u</math> is a vector in <math>\mathbb R^d</math> and <math>\mathbf{I_C}</math> is the indicator function of the set <math>C</math>.{{sfn|Sato|1999|pp=37–38}}

A Lèvy process characteristic function has the same structure but with <math>\gamma_t =t\gamma, \nu_t = t\nu</math> and <math>A_t = At</math> with <math>\gamma</math> a vector in <math>\mathbb R^d</math>, <math>A</math> a positive definite matrix in <math>\mathbb R^{d \times d}</math>  and  <math>\nu</math> is a measure on <math>\mathbb R^d</math>.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=95}}

== Existence and uniqueness in law of additive process==
The following result together with the ''Lévy–Khintchine formula'' characterizes the additive process.

Let <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> be an additive process on <math>\mathbb R^d</math>. Then, its infinitely divisible distribution is such that:
# For all <math>t</math>, <math>A_t</math> is a positive definite matrix.
# <math>\gamma_0=0, A_0=0, \nu_0=0</math> and for all <math>s, t</math> is such that <math>s<t</math>, <math>A_t-A_s</math> is a positive definite matrix and <math>\nu_t(B)\geq \nu_s(B)</math> for every <math>B</math> in <math>\mathbf{B}(\mathbb R^d)</math>.
#If <math> s\to t</math> <math>\gamma_s\to \gamma_t, A_s \to A_t</math>  and <math>\nu_s(B)\to \nu_t(B)</math> every <math>B</math> in <math>\mathbf{B}(\mathbb R^d)</math>, <math>0\not\in B</math>.

Conversely for family of infinitely divisible distributions characterized by a generating triplet  <math>(\gamma_t, A_t, \nu_t)</math> that satisfies 1, 2 and 3, it exists an additive process  <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> with this distribution.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=458}}{{sfn|Sato|1999|p=63}}

== Subclass of additive process ==
===Additive Logistic Process===
Family of additive processes with [[generalized logistic distribution]]. Their 5 parameters characteristic function is 
: <math> \operatorname E \left[e^{iuX_t}\right] =  \left(\frac{B(\alpha_t+i \sigma_t u, \beta_t- i \sigma u )}{B(\alpha_t, \beta_t)} \right)^{\delta_t} e^{ i \mu_t u}\;\;. </math>
Two subcases of additive logistic process are the symmetric logistic additive process with standard [[logistic distribution]] (<math>\alpha_t=1 </math>, <math>\beta_t=1 </math>, <math>\delta_t=1 </math>) and the conjugate-power Dagum additive process with [[Dagum distribution]] (<math>\alpha_t=1 </math>, <math>\beta_t=1-\sigma(t) </math>, <math>\alpha_t=1 </math>).
 
The function <math>\mu_t </math> can always be chosen s.t. the additive process is a [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale]].{{sfn|Carr|Torricelli|2021|p= 698}}

===Additive Normal Tempered Stable Process===
Extension of the Lévy normal tempered stable processes; some well-known Lévy normal tempered stable processes have [[normal-inverse Gaussian distribution]] and the [[variance-gamma distribution]]. 
Additive normal tempered stable processes{{sfn|Azzone|Baviera|2022|p= 503}} have the same characteristic function of Lévy normal tempered stable processes but with time dependent parameters <math>\sigma_t</math> (the level of the volatility), <math>k_t</math> (the variance of jumps) and <math>\eta_t</math> (linked to the skew):
: <math> \operatorname E \left[e^{iuX_t}\right] = {\cal L}_t \left(iu \left(\frac{1}{2}+\eta_t \right)\sigma_t^2+\frac{u^2\sigma^2_t}{2};\;k_t,\;\alpha \right)e^{iu\varphi_tt}, </math>
where
: <math> \ln {\cal L}_t \left(u;\;k_t,\;\alpha\right) :=
\begin{cases} 
	\displaystyle \frac{t}{k_t}
	\displaystyle \frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}
	\left \{1-		\left(1+\frac{u \; k_t}{1-\alpha}\right)^\alpha \right \} & \mbox{if } \; 0< \alpha < 1 \\[4mm]
	\displaystyle -\frac{t}{k_t}
	\ln \left(1+u \; k_t\right)  & \mbox{if } \; \alpha = 0 \end{cases}   </math>
The function <math>\varphi_t </math> can always be chosen s.t. the additive process is a  [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale]].{{sfn|Azzone|Baviera|2022|p= 503}}

=== Additive Subordinator===
A positive non decreasing additive process <math>\{S_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> with values in <math>\mathbb R</math> is an additive [[subordinator (mathematics)|subordinator]].
An additive subordinator is a [[semimartingale]] (thanks to the fact that it is not decreasing) and it is always possible to rewrite its [[Laplace transform]] as

: <math>\operatorname E\left[ e^{-u S_t} \right] = \exp\left(u b_t + \int_{\mathbb R^d} (e^{i u x}-1) \nu_t(dx)\right). </math>{{sfn|Li|Li|Mendoza-Arriaga|2016|pp= 5–6}}

It is possible to use additive subordinator to time-change a Lévy process obtaining a new class of additive processes.{{sfn|Li|Li|Mendoza-Arriaga|2016|p= 1}}

=== Sato Process ===
An additive [[self-similar process]] <math>\{Z_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> is called Sato process.{{sfn|Eberlein|Madan|2009|p= 5}}
It is possible to construct a Sato process from a Lévy process  <math>\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}</math> such that <math>Z_t</math> has the same law of <math>t^hX_1</math>.

An example is the variance gamma SSD, the Sato process obtained starting from the [[variance gamma process]].

The characteristic function of the Variance gamma at time <math>t=1</math> is

: <math> \operatorname E \left[e^{iuX_1}\right] = \left(\frac{1}{1-iu\theta\nu+0.5\sigma^2\nu u^2}\right)^{1/\nu}, </math>

where <math>\theta, \nu</math> and <math>\sigma</math> are positive constant.

The characteristic function of the variance gamma SSD is

: <math> \operatorname E \left[e^{iuZ_t}\right] = \left(\frac{1}{1-iut^h\theta\nu+0.5\sigma^2\nu u^2t^2h}\right)^{1/\nu}</math>{{sfn|Carr|Geman|Madan|Yor|2007|p= 39}}

== Simulation ==
Simulation of Additive process is computationally efficient thanks to the independence of increments. The additive process increments can be simulated separately and simulation can also be parallelized.{{sfn|Eberlein|Madan|2009|}}

===Jump simulation===
	Jump simulation is a generalization to the class of  additive processes of the jump simulation technique developed for Lévy  processes.
	The method is based on truncating small jumps below a certain threshold and  simulating the finite number of independent jumps. 
	Moreover, Gaussian approximation can be applied to replace small jumps with a diffusive term. It is also possible to use the [[Ziggurat algorithm]] to speed up the simulation of jumps.{{sfn|Eberlein|Madan|2009|p= 19}}

===Characteristic function inversion===
Simulation of Lévy process via characteristic function inversion is a well established technique in the literature.{{sfn|Ballotta|Kyriakou|2014|p= 1}}
This technique  can be extended to additive processes. The key idea is obtaining an approximation of the [[cumulative distribution function]] (CDF) by inverting the [[characteristic function]]. The inversion speed is enhanced by the use of the [[Fast Fourier transform]]. Once the approximation of the CDF is available is it possible to simulate an additive process increment just by simulating a uniform random variable. The method has similar computational cost as simulating a standard geometric Brownian motion.{{sfn|Azzone|Baviera|2023|pp=1-5}}

==Applications==
=== Quantitative finance ===
Lévy process is used to model the log-returns of market prices. Unfortunately, the ''stationarity '' of the increments does not reproduce correctly market data. A Lévy process fit well [[call option]] and [[put option]] prices ([[Volatility smile|implied volatility]]) for a single expiration date but is unable to fit options prices with different maturities ([[Volatility (finance)#Implied volatility parametrisation|volatility surface]]). The additive process introduces a ''deterministic'' non-stationarity that allows it to fit all expiration dates.{{sfn|Tankov|Cont|2003|p=454}}

A four-parameters Sato process (self-similar additive process) can reproduce correctly the volatility surface (3% error on the [[S&P 500 Index|S&P 500]]  equity market). This order of magnitude of error is usually obtained using models with 6-10 parameters to fit market data.{{sfn|Carr|Geman|Madan|Yor|2007|p= 32}} A self-similar process correctly describes market data because of its flat [[skewness]] and excess [[kurtosis]]; empirical studies had observed this behavior in market skewness and excess kurtosis.{{sfn|Carr|Geman|Madan|Yor|2007|p= 37}}
Some of the processes that fit option prices with a 3% error are  VGSSD, NIGSSD, MXNRSSD obtained from variance gamma process, normal inverse Gaussian process and Meixner process.{{sfn|Carr|Geman|Madan|Yor|2007|pp= 39–42}}

Additive normal tempered stable processes fit  accurately equity market data ( error below 0.8% on the [[S&P 500 Index|S&P 500]]  equity market) specifically for short maturities. These family of processes reproduces very well also the equity market implied volatility skew.
Moreover, an interesting power scaling characteristic arises in calibrated parameters <math>k_t=\bar{k}t^\beta</math> and <math>\eta_t=\bar{\eta}t^\delta</math>. There is statistical evidence that  <math>\beta=1</math>
and <math>\delta=-1/2</math>.{{sfn|Azzone|Baviera|2022|pp= 506-508}}

Lévy subordination is used to construct new Lévy processes (for example variance gamma process and normal inverse Gaussian process).  There is a large number of financial applications of processes constructed by Lévy subordination. An additive process built via additive subordination maintains the analytical tractability of a process built via Lévy subordination but it reflects better the time-inhomogeneus structure of market data.{{sfn|Li|Li|Mendoza-Arriaga|2016|pp= 3}} Additive subordination is applied to the commodity market{{sfn|Li|Li|Mendoza-Arriaga|2016|p= 17}} and to VIX options.{{sfn|Li|Li|Zhang|2017|p= 1}}

===Digital image processing===
An estimator based on the minimum of an additive process can be applied to image processing. Such estimator aims to distinguish between real signal and noise in the picture pixels.{{sfn|Bhattacharya|Brockwell|1976|p= 71}}
